static_traits.name: Zhang Mingyu
static_traits.family_status: Her husband works at a telecom company
static_traits.social_status: Conflicts with husband and friends over driving-related topics;though supported by husband and a few close friends,they reportedly do not yet fully understand the distress
static_traits.medical_history: A minor car accident several years ago;no similar psychological issues before;has not yet received psychotherapy;No major physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly,able to describe trigger situations and automatic thoughts;uses many emotional terms('always''the worst');skeptical about cognitive Intervention but willing to try,fairly cooperative

basic_info.main_problem: Feels frustrated every time I drive, and this frustration affects my mood and daily life.
basic_info.core_demands: Driving-related frustration and stress have become hard to bear,affecting overall well-being and causing Relationship tension;hoping for support and guidance to manage these feelings;not wanting to dread/detest driving every day.
growth_experiences: Experienced a minor car accident several years ago,and began fearing driving afterwards.Initial stress was moderate,but over time it developed into Anticipation of frustration before every drive,even for short trips.Driving alone,especially during rush hour or heavy traffic,easily triggers intense frustration and Anxiety.Tried relaxation techniques and avoiding driving as much as possible,but the problem persists,and discussing travel with husband and friends triggers conflicts.Though having a husband and a few close friends to confide in,they feel these people do not yet fully understand the difficulty.

core_beliefs: The world (road environment) is dangerous and full of threats
I cannot effectively control my emotions and their consequences while driving

special_situations.event: Driving alone, stuck in traffic during the evening rush hour
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am delayed by traffic, it means the consequences will be very bad, I will lose control, and everything will turn bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to force emotions down with relaxation techniques, or simply avoids going out at peak times / reduces driving
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will become a disaster; I will be late and the consequences will be severe.

special_situations.event: The moment of getting back in the car to drive after a car accident or just gripping the steering wheel
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I drive again, I will very likely have another accident; driving inevitably involves danger
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding driving whenever possible,having others drive instead;if must drive,monitoring road conditions with high tension

special_situations.event: When any planned trip requires driving oneself
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If driving cannot go completely smoothly,it is utterly terrible;as long as I drive I will surely get frustrated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Before setting out, makes the worst psychological preparations and strengthens avoidance tendencies, reduces driving frequency
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Every time I drive it will be terrible; I will definitely be frustrated.

special_situations.event: Seeing other drivers cut in or block while in traffic congestion
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not drive the way I expect,they are targeting me,deliberately making me uncomfortable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Blaming discomfort on others,getting angry,complaining to release tension and gain a sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are deliberately making me late, working against me.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain a sense of safety and control in driving and travel, and to be truly understood and supported by significant others
core_conflict.fear: Fear of another accident,losing control,or being ignored and negated,thus falling into helplessness and shame
defense_goal: Reducing Anxiety and powerlessness through Avoids driving and external attribution
Maintains a subjective sense of control and safe distance through anger and blame

object_relations.self_representation: A trapped victim who is misunderstood and powerless to control
object_relations.object_representation: Others who do not understand and dismiss feelings(such as husband/friends,'others' on the road)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites Identifying automatic thoughts and trying cognitive restructuring
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experienced as minimizing one's real dilemma,worrying about being dismissed again by 'ineffective advice'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Listing past experiences of ineffective attempts in a rationally questioning tone,emphasizing 'not applicable at present',with a restrained but defensive tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others(including counselor/spouse) offer 'relax/calm down' advice or remain silent while listening
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting inner powerlessness and anger as the external attitude of 'you do not understand/are negating me'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use generalized and blaming expressions(such as 'none of you understand'),raising vocal intensity,turning to complaining about others' behavior to seek allies.

manifestations: Feeling that husband and friends do not yet truly understand one's driving distress
Subjectively experiences traffic as 'everyone is against me'
When Driving alone,unease and Sense of frustration significantly worsen
Avoids driving due to Fear and frustration,with action choices 'bound' by roads and emotions
Experiencing intense uncontrollability and restriction in the face of congestion
outcomes: Shrinking life radius and diminished sense of autonomy
Rigid pursuit of control further Reinforcement negative experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Attributing anger and powerlessness in congestion to 'others deliberately targeting me'
Responding to Supportive intervention in counseling with 'you do not understand me'

positive_force: Has social support from husband and a few friends
Willing to seek help and enter counseling,able to be self-aware of automatic thoughts to some degree
Has actively tried self-help methods like relaxation techniques
Able to acknowledge the objectivity of peak-hour traffic congestion (can serve as an entry point for cognitive reappraisal)
negative_force: Marked cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing,overgeneralization,personalization,predicting the future,black-and-white thinking
Conditioned fear and hypervigilance brought by the car accident experience
The Avoids driving coping style maintains the problem cycle
Difficulty with emotion regulation, easily angered and externalizing the sense of control onto others / the environment

target_behavior.behavior: Intense frustration and anger while driving,with a tendency to Avoids driving
antecedent: During rush hour or heavy traffic
The moment of gripping the steering wheel, ready to depart
Recalling a past minor car accident
target_behavior.core_reason: Heightened threat appraisal of driving risks and consequences after the accident,accompanied by cognitive biases such as catastrophizing,overgeneralization,predicting the future,personalization,leading to emotional dysregulation
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome stimuli(congestion,sense of losing control,worry about another accident) and gaining brief subjective control through anger/external attribution
target_behavior.consequence: Affects daily life and emotional stability; conflicts with her husband and friends; reduced driving leads to restricted travel
